utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. At the outset of today's hearing, the Chamber would like to raise two procedural matters. First, the Chamber notes that we are not scheduled to sit on Monday, the 15th of November 2010. Taking into account the length of the Prosecution case and the necessity of an expeditious trial, the Chamber would like to sit on that day because at least two judges are available. Yesterday, the Chamber has contacted the parties and communicated its intention. Now, the Chamber would like to hear from the parties if they are prepared to sit on the 15th of November and whether the OTP is able to call a witness for that day. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, and good afternoon to Your Honours, good afternoon to the Defence, and good afternoon, everyone. Mr. President, we have thus far been able to accommodate some of the last-minute scheduling changes and alterations. Unfortunately, in this case we are unable to fill that day with a witness primarily for the following two reasons: One is the testimony of the witness for whom the Trial Chamber issued a Rule 54 subpoena, the videographer does not appear to be co-operative at the moment. We have been in contact with him and so far the indications are that he is being non-compliant with the Trial Chamber's subpoena. We intend to re-establish contact to find out just how firm that non-compliance will be. The bottom line is that we don't think we can count on him being here next week, so it is difficult enough as it is to try to then -- now we are in the position of pulling other available witnesses to fill gaps, and we will be lucky if we can fill next week, so with respect to Monday, the 15th, that will not be possible. The second reason that is preventing us from having additional gap fillers is we are having and encountering difficulties with a number of our witnesses who just cannot make it any more. They just don't have the emotional and psychic and wherewithal to endure testifying for the third or fourth time, and I'm speaking primarily of survivors who we have placed on the witness list and, in a couple of cases, who have been the subject of motions to convert their testimony to Rule 92 bis witnesses. And we are finding that more and more witnesses are in the same position, that they simply cannot take it any more. And we also have the same situation with some non-survivor witnesses as well. So right now, the confluence of those two factors places us in the position where we don't have, I don't think, anybody to fill that day on the 15th. Were Mr. Stojkovic to be available it would be a different story, but we are now in the position of having to fill possibly three days next week, and I can tell you what we have in mind for you for that week. The first is we have Mr. Blasczyk, ever our gap filler, available to testify concerning what we refer to as the road book. In the Popovic case, Mr. Blaszczyk testified for a couple of days concerning the Zoran Petrovic video. Mr. Petrovic was a Belgrade-based journalist who during a trip to Srebrenica on the 13th and afterwards videotaped events, and the Trial Chamber is no doubt familiar with portions of that video which have been shown recently. Given particularly that the Trial Chamber has recently been on the site visit and has a better idea now of where some of these locations are, it's as good a time as any to present this testimony during which we have a full colour book of video stills from that video. Mr. Blasczyk explains exactly what's going on in these stills and where, more importantly, along that video and along the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje in particular certain events are taking place. We think that that testimony is very helpful for understanding better the context and the location. So I am working to get him ready and myself ready to put him on next week. I can tell you that the two most relevant exhibits are P1251, which has been marked for identification in connection with Mr. Petrovic's proposed Rule 92 -- I can't remember whether it was ter or bis but it's been accepted under one of those rules by the Trial Chamber and it's been provisionally admitted and that is in e-court, but again we will have the actual full colour versions for the Trial Chamber to look at during the course of Mr. Blasczyk's testimony so we don't have to rely on necessarily e-court which is a little bit smaller. The second exhibit in connection with Mr. Blasczyk's proposed testimony is 65 ter 2178 which is an interactive CD containing the -- much of the same information and video footage but allows the user to rotate the images in a 360 degree manner so that you truly feel like and can orient oneself on the spot and that incorporates latter day filming of these same positions where Your Honours recently visited. Again, we think that that's helpful for really getting a feel of how things were happening during these events on the road. So that's the first gap filler we have. The second gap filler -- oh, I beg your pardon, actually the first gap filler that we are trying to obtain is the return of Colonel Egbers. He has indicated that he is available for Tuesday, the 9th. We are in the process of seeing whether there are Dutch interpreters available for that day. If he's not or if the interpreters are not available we will start with Mr. Blaszczyk, he's a sure thing, Colonel Egbers is not a sure thing right now. We will update everybody when we have more information. If we still have a gap towards the end of the week, we have Ms. Gallagher available to return to testify about the -- what we refer to as the Muslim ID book, which is a book of video stills of individual Muslim men who were filmed, in some cases by Mr. Petrovic and in some cases by others, at various points during the deportation from Potocari. The point of the book is to identify, from those video stills, individual Muslim men and boys who did not survive and whose remains have been identified in various mass graves or who otherwise remain missing on the ICRC missing list, and Ms. Gallagher is available to explain how this book was put together and the foundation for the contents of the book. So I think we should be able to have adequate witnesses to fill the week next week should the subpoena not be complied with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just for better understanding, Mr. Thayer, you mentioned three witnesses, Mr. Blaszczyk, Mr. Egbers, and Ms. Gallagher. And you will schedule them for next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In order to conclude their testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, in the case of Mr. Blaszczyk and Ms. Gallagher, they would be beginning new testimony. I don't know how far we will get, for example, with Mr. Blaszczyk testimony overall, whether we will finish cross, for example, but the idea is to at least get them started on that new testimony, if we -- in addition if we get Colonel Egbers in. Right now we are operating under the presumption that the subpoena's witness will not be available next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you talking about next week or the following week?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Next week because next week we had a subpoenaed witness scheduled and then the following week we had another -- the second subpoenaed witness scheduled to testify. So I'm speaking of the videographer for next week and the other witness for the following week, that is, the week of the 15th that is the subject of the Trial Chamber's inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the testimony of the relevant witnesses will not be finished next week, why is it not possible to sit on the 15th? Monday, the 15th? It's the following week.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That would be possible, Mr. President, if that testimony is not completed. I expect that if cross-examination is started, if the Defence is in a position to begin cross-examination of Mr. Blaszczyk or Ms. Gallagher that they would be finished by next week. If not, yes, I think we would be available to sit on the 15th, with those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what is your position to sit on the 15th of November, the Monday of the following week?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no problem with that at all, if it is in the afternoon, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In that case, we should schedule a hearing on Monday, the 15th of November in the afternoon, pending the question if the examination of the witnesses we are talking about is not finished. Please continue, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just wanted to add one thing, Mr. President. With respect to the subpoenaed witness who is scheduled for next week, I just wanted to give the Trial Chamber an idea of where we may be headed with that. Should the witness continue to affirm his non-compliance with the Trial Chamber's subpoena, we will be applying to the Trial Chamber for an order in lieu of contempt indictment to be issued by the Trial Chamber along with a warrant for that witness's arrest, to force him to comply with the valid order of this Trial Chamber for his testimony before the Court, and again this is witness number 185 we are speaking of. It is the Prosecution's view that having that order, those proceedings, emanate from the Trial Chamber will be the most expeditious and direct way of accomplishing the transfer of this witness to the Tribunal and obtaining ultimately his testimony which is what we want. So again, the Trial Chamber can expect that application should he continue to exhibit his desire not to comply with the Trial Chamber's subpoena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: After having received such an application, the Chamber will take that into account and consider it. Thank you very much. Now, I would like to raise the second topic. During the testimony of witness Egbers on the 1st and 2nd November, earlier this week, the following exhibits were admitted without a B/C/S translation. First, the Exhibit P1149, this is an UNMO situation report, and secondly, the Exhibits P1150 and P1153. These are chapters of reports of the Netherlands Institute for War Documentation. In the Popovic case these exhibits have been tendered by the Defence and admitted without a B/C/S translation. The Chamber would like to inquire with you, Mr. Tolimir, whether you intend to use these documents during his continued cross-examination of -- your continues cross-examination of Witness Egbers and whether you therefore require these documents to be translated or if you would, in this particular instance, waive your right to receive this evidence in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence shall not waive its right to find out what is the content of those documents, given the fact that I do not know the language. And secondly, they have been extremely important, they are important for this Defence, they have been important to other defence teams, and we should like to ask and would appreciate receiving an early translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In this case, the documents I have mentioned are only marked for identification and not admitted yet, pending translation. Thank you very much. If there are no other matters to discuss, the witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is being brought in we have some updated translations to inform the Court about. We have P365b, P398b, P375b, P382b, P433, P407d, P407c, P606, P618, P843c, P963, P1304, and P1227b.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These exhibits are now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and that concludes my business before the Chamber this afternoon. May I be excused for the remainor of the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, have a nice evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you as well, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Gajic, you wanted to raise something too? Mr. Gajic, I saw you on your feet. Nothing, okay. Good afternoon, Mr. Janc, welcome back to the courtroom. May I remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we are still in the stage of cross-examination, if I recall correctly. Mr. Tolimir, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I great all present, I wish God's peace to this house and that this case be concluded in keeping with God's will and not mine. I great Mr. Janc and I bid him welcome in our midst.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: At the conclusion of the last day of your testimony, I asked you whether anyone, before this Court, and it was unclear whether a convict or an accused, it was unclear on that day, whether anyone had been convicted of murders in Trnovo before this Court.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember this question, yes. And I think I -- that I have provided you with an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will tell you what your answer was: "Yes, these were the only murders in regard of which indictments were brought against those who were accused for events in Srebrenica." On the basis of your answer, I cannot actually gather whether anyone had been convicted before this Court for those murders. And you also said: "I would have to consult the relevant judgements."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. And I consulted the Popovic judgement in relation to this issue, and I found out that the individuals were convicted for this crime and it is -- it is concluded in the JCE common purpose issue and it is discussed there. So I can confirm that the individuals were convicted for this crime, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As you have now just said that it was a part of the JCE, can you tell us on what grounds are all other indictees accused of the so-called joint criminal enterprise associated with those who committed the murders in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you, good afternoon, everybody. Mr. President, I object to the question. It is true that the convictions that arose in other cases with respect to these killings does have some relevance in this case. However, the witness's knowledge about the legal basis supporting those convictions, or even the factual circumstances underlying those convictions, is of little relevance, if any, to this case and, in particular, to the specific issues toward which the cross-examination is directed. The witness testified, in particular, with respect to the provenance and authenticity of videotape footage. Part of the videotape footage encompassed the crimes about which General Tolimir is legitimately inquiring about on cross-examination. However, whether or not an individual -- whether or not this particular witness knows the legal basis upon which a conviction involving those crimes was founded in another proceeding, in another judgement, is really of marginal relevance to his testimony and marginal relevance to the issues before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if you want to find out on which reasons and which legal basis somebody was convicted, it is very simple to find out by reading this judgement. I think it can't be helpful to use this witness to find out if somebody was sentenced according to JCE membership or something else. You should focus on the knowledge of this witness and the facts he can provide you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Presiding Judge. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. I accept everything that you said. My purpose is to obtain the truth but I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you explore who ordered the crimes in Trnovo to be committed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was trying to get this information, reviewing the documentation and various materials we have -- the OTP is having in possession, and more than I thought here during my testimony I couldn't find.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When taping this video, it is obvious from the transcript, the cameraman says, and I quote, and that is page 3 -- pages 3 to 13, it is -- it is Exhibit P1024, page 13, line 15, and can that be brought up on the screen for the benefit of the witness, please? I apologise, it is page 3 of a total of 13. Thank you, but we see the document but we don't see page 3. Could page 3, line 15, be brought up, please? Here we can see it in English, Aleksandar is showing this to me, the first word is "cameraman," and he says: "Zekan, go quickly, turn the truck around and bring it back. My battery has died on me." Thank you. Do you remember that he said that in the video clip that you showed us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember this portion of the video, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that he wanted a new battery in order to be able to record the killings? Is that what he meant when he said, "My battery is dead"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That's what he meant, and you can see immediately after that on the video that the truck goes away, and according to the statements we have obtained from the individuals, that truck driver was going back to pick up another battery. So -- and since this spot was not far away, two to three kilometres away from their base, the truck driver was back later on and this individual replaced the battery. And you can hear later on, when the execution is taking place, that battery is again dying, so we will see his voice again saying, the cameraman is saying, also something in that sense that the battery is -- is -- also this battery is dying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing in mind that you studied the video clip and that you looked at it carefully and you heard him ask for a battery, can you tell from the video clip that the executions were being delayed while waiting for the camera to come back with a new battery?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say the camera was always there. The camera didn't go back to their base and return back. The camera and the cameraman was always there, only the person, one of them, went back to their base to pick up a new battery, and then this individual returned back and the battery was changed. And then, yes, we can say that that was the reason that the execution was delayed because they were waiting for the new battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting my mistake. I said did they wait for the camera and I should have said did they wait for the battery. Does this point to a conclusion that somebody ordered the camera person to document the execution? Did somebody instruct him to record the executions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. And when we -- I mean the OTP interviewed him he confirmed that fact, that he was ordered to film the execution, and not only that, during the -- on the film itself you can see that one of the Skorpion's members turns back to him and he's asking him that he needs to film this, otherwise -- and if the film will not be okay, he would also be killed. Something in that sense. So he was ordered, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the OTP investigate where such an order could have come from? Did the OTP learn anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP tried to obtain as much information as possible on how this incident took place, who ordered it, when it took place, and all the circumstances regarding this event. I can confirm that we didn't get everything what we wanted so -- and during information I provided here during my testimony is all I can say what -- what the Prosecution is having in their possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Two witnesses, as you have just said it yourself, and we can see this in document P1023, say that the cameraman was ordered to film the executions. Did the OTP investigate who had the motive to do that? Did it try to establish who that person was, or what position such a person might have occupied?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the OTP did investigate that fact, and my answer to your question would be very similar to my previous one so that for sure we didn't get all the information regarding this incident, in particular what you are asking me who was the main individual who ordered these killings, I mean from the higher level military or within the police organisation. So -- but individuals who were involved in this incident are unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you have the document in front of you, and you can look the fifth line in the third paragraph, where two persons say that an order had been issued to record the executions, wouldn't it be desirable to find out who had the motive to issue such an order? Maybe that would also shed the light on all the other killings in Srebrenica. Do you know if anybody has investigated that, and if they did, do you know what the results of such an investigation may have been?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP wanted to get as much information as possible, as I emphasised many times so far, and more than we got, we didn't -- we didn't get. So of course, it is of our interest to find out what was the motive, what was -- who was standing behind every particular crime, and in this case, the executors are known to the OTP and what is also known who are the victims, it is also known where this incidents took place, how these victims were most probably brought from Srebrenica area to this area, and these are information which OTP obtained during the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: However, before we draw any general conclusions about the responsibility of the so-called joint criminal enterprise, and since two persons here are saying that an order had been issued, and they were all arrested, including the one who gave the order to them, did you try to talk to that person in order to find out where the original order for the executions to be documented, to be filmed, had come from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, the OTP talked to this individual, and if I'm not wrong, he didn't tell us where did the order come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It would be very important to know whether he himself confirmed that he was acting upon somebody's order. Did he confirm that? But he didn't want to name the person who issued that order. Is that a fair representation of what you just said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this person, what actually he said to us, but I'm sure he didn't name the individuals, but for other details you are asking me now I would rather consult his statement once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At trial in Belgrade, did that individual perhaps name the person who had issued the order? Did he perhaps state that somebody had ordered him to film the executions in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My response would be the same. I would need to consult his Belgrade statement also, but if you have this statement and this portion of his interview, I can -- I can take a look and I can agree that this statement we have received from the Serbian authorities, and I can confirm and agree that this is what he said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have the right to testify here and I don't have the same amount of materials as you do. I'm asking you whether he said that it had been ordered to him to execute the men and to record the executions on a videotape. Just say "yes" or "no" and that will be the last of my questions about that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think if my recollection is correct, that the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If he said yes, then a new issue may be raised here. There was therefore somebody, before the killings took place, that -- who wanted the killings to take place, who ordered those killings. Did you investigate whether anybody had the motive to order those killings and to order those killings to be documented on a videotape?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to our investigation, I've already told you how far did we get with the investigation. And many, many different options are possible, always. And, yes, that would be my response to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, or me, for that matter, whether you know if Mr. Medic is going to testify before this Trial Chamber and in these proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am sure he's not going to testify, and this individual is the -- he was the chief of the Skorpions unit and he was convicted in Belgrade, and he is serving his sentence right now there. So the Prosecution in this case did not call him as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you investigate if anybody from the leadership of Republika Srpska and the Army of Republika Srpska had a motive to order such an execution and document it by a film camera? Was anybody in either the political or military leadership interested in doing that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such investigation being done, so I'm not aware, so I think I cannot respond to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you yourself are an investigator, could you tell us whether it would be necessary to investigate that, since the whole matter is treated as a joint criminal enterprise? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's usually necessary to investigate as much as possible. So -- but sometimes it's impossible to do that, and there are different factors for that. So in general sense, I can -- I can agree with you that it's important to find out, you know, who is behind each and every crime committed, and I don't see any difference here, with this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since the crimes were committed by individuals who were outside of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you received the document from Sarajevo which is in the centre of Bosnia and Herzegovina, did you investigate whether the order issuer perhaps had been located in Sarajevo? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can be a little bit more clear regarding which document you are now talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, the film was made by a cameraman and other persons who belonged to the Skorpion group, a group that was active outside of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you received it from a reliable source from Sarajevo, a part under the control of BiH. Did you investigate the possibility that the murders and their recording may have been ordered from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is now a misinterpretation. We never -- we never said and according to the declaration we can see on our screen, it's clear how the Prosecution obtained this video, when, from which person, it says here of course as a confidential source, and this source is not a member of ABiH. He is a member of the Skorpions unit, and I think it's quite clear how the Prosecution obtained this video and from whom. So it has nothing to do with the BiH army of BiH or any other BiH federal institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 16 of today's transcript, line 13, or starting with line 12, you state that: "So the Prosecution in this case did not call him as a witness." Do you know if he has been called as a witness in another case before the Tribunal? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I'm not mistaken he hasn't been called by any other Trial Chamber, simply due to the fact that he was arrested in 2005 already, soon after this video was introduced in this -- at the ICTY courtroom for its first time during the Milosevic trial and he has been arrested after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, if you'd look at paragraph 7 in the document that's before you now, if you look at line 1, in paragraph 7, you will see that it says here, "I went to Sarajevo." That's the senior OTP officer who says that. And then he speaks about the money that had to be approved for him to obtain that. And then in paragraph 8 he says: "Before leaving Sarajevo for The Hague, the intermediary arranged with us to meet a certain person and that meeting was supposed to take place a week later." Bearing that in mind, in my previous question when I suggested that order issuer may have been from Sarajevo and you said no, how can you say no if you didn't investigate the matter if you received the film from Sarajevo? Can you tell us what is the link between Sarajevo and the perpetrators of the crime? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think the witness has already answered the question. The declaration speaks for itself as to the issues that are being put by General Tolimir at this time, and it does not speak to the circumstances under which the initial order to carry out the executions or to videotape the executions were issued, and so I just don't see that it's a relevant question based upon this document. If there is some other information the general seeks to obtain, I think that's fair, but I don't think that emanates from a review of this documents or anything this document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I think the witness is capable to answer this question, especially the last part: "How can you say no if you didn't investigate the matter, if you received the film from Sarajevo? Can you tell us what is the link between Sarajevo and the perpetrators of the crime?" I think this part of the question can be answered by the witness. Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Indeed, the Prosecution obtained this video in Sarajevo, but from -- again from a person who came to Sarajevo, so that individual just wanted to get in contact with the OTP investigators in Sarajevo for some reason, and how I'm able to conclude that is based mainly on this declaration and that's more or less -- I mean in relation to this place where we got the video. As per your question how far Sarajevo is from this location, I think it's around 30 to 50 kilometres south from Sarajevo. That's where Trnovo is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything in any of the documents that would point to that conclusion? You say, "I concluded." Is there anything in the documents that would points to that conclusion? I don't see any such thing in the documents disclosed to us by the OTP. Maybe you have something else, a different statement, or something of the sort. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One is this declaration, then we have also the statement of this individual himself who provided us with this tape, and the second source where I can see which -- where something was obtained is also our internal OTP record. When we obtain some evidence, we make a little synopsis of how we get the stuff, from which source and from where, and this is additional source where I can see from where certain evidence was obtained or found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the material disclosed to us by the OTP, we can only see that it is P345, in which case we are not able to know the details that you're talking about. I apologise if I'm asking you something that we are not supposed to know. However, I think it would be very important to know whether there is any link between Sarajevo and the organisers of that crime. Thank you. My next question is this: Do you know, did you investigate, why the persons had been brought to Trnovo and murdered there in front of the camera? And we can see on the footage that the cameraman was threatened by that other person who told him if you don't get it right, we will kill you as well. So why did these individuals who were murdered have to be brought to Trnovo in the first place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation itself didn't come to a clear conclusion regarding this fact. So the information we have, and based on the evidence we have, we are -- we may conclude that these individuals are the victims from Srebrenica because of the fact they left Srebrenica enclave after its fall, and we know that they were transported from Srebrenica area to Trnovo soon after the fall of Srebrenica, and that they were killed there. They were handed over to this Skorpion unit and killed by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just told us we know that they were brought from Srebrenica and handed over to the Skorpion unit. Does it mean that the Skorpions had not actually captured them but that they were brought over and handed over to them in that place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From documents, statements the OTP has, we can conclude yes that's the case. They were brought there by bus or truck from Srebrenica area and handed over to the Skorpions unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the first part of your testimony, you said that there is a statement by their close relatives who stated that they were attempting a breakthrough with rest of the people in the column and that was the last news that they had of them. Is that what you stated in the first part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the individuals we see on this video, one of those six, was breaking through the -- this area with his brother-in-law, and he identified him as the person with whom he left Srebrenica together after its fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this indicate that those persons left Srebrenica with a column which was attempting to break through, and do you have any witness testifying to the fact that they had been returned to Srebrenica again? Because a while ago you said that they had been brought from Srebrenica to Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. What I meant with Srebrenica is not the Srebrenica town itself but the area of Srebrenica, which is much wider, you know. I would rather say the area -- the way where the column was passing towards the north, so the wider area of Srebrenica, I should say, so they were brought from this area down to Trnovo. So we have witnesses of course, and one of these -- at least one of these witnesses, I think, will also testify here and will confirm that one of these victims left Srebrenica after its fall, heading towards free territory, through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As you know all this, do you know where they were arrested, the exact location? Were they arrested and then handed over to the person who took them to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this information is not known to the OTP. I made searches on these individuals to see if any additional information or documentation is available in our collection, in OTP collection, in order to confirm at least something where and when they were captured but I couldn't find any information regarding this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know the time of their arrest and the exact time of their execution? Does the OTP know these facts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the time, regarding the time of their capture, I can say it's not known to the Prosecution. Based on all the facts which Prosecution is aware of, it should be after the fall of Srebrenica in July of 1995. And according to the statements the OTP obtained from those individuals involved in these killings it should be -- the killing took place in sometime in July also of 1995. And there is one document which one of the witnesses the OTP interviewed confirmed, and this document is from 20 of July, and this witness confirmed that based on this document, the Skorpion unit was pulled back from the Trnovo area so they were not there any more. So this incident, based on this fact, should take place between 12th and 20th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As this is very important, because of the individuals who are being charged with this, to know the exact time, place, and manner, do you have any other information about any other participants in the event apart from those who have been convicted? Any other members from the Army of Republika Srpska or any other members who participated in their arrest, in their taking to that location, in their killing? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We -- so far we don't have any additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a while ago that one witness testified in this case. I do not remember any of the witnesses to the murder having testified in this case. Can you jog my memory, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, the witness said one person will testify in this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm I was referring to the witnesses who is coming, still coming to testify here, so he will testify.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would appreciate it very much if you told us whether you investigated what role this group had in Trnovo apart from that killing. Did they participate in any combat action? Is there any reference to them or to any of them in any of the combat reports of the time? I'm talking about their combat activities in the Trnovo sector.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were involved in combat activities in this Trnovo area, Trnovo battlefield as they called it at the time. And they were supporting the VRS and Republika Srpska MUP units in that area at the time. So -- and basically that's why they came or they were deployed to this area in early or late June of 1995, and one of -- I haven't seen any of their reports. I would -- I mean the Skorpion unit report I haven't seen any of those reports, but what we can see and we have seen also here in this courtroom is, for example, the report from Ljubisa Borovcanin on 1st of July when he's reporting that there are combat activities which are performed together with these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, is this document 1D288 that you're referring to? And could we please have it brought up in e-court, if it is indeed the one that you are referring to? It is Borovcanin, is consolidated report on activities from the 12th to the 20th. Is that the one you are talking about? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this case I was referring to the one from 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall call that document from the 1st of July, 1995. It is document P1025, if that is the one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P1025 brought up on the screen, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We now have that document in front of us. Can you tell us where there is reference here to their activities and to their participation in combat?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's within the first paragraph, that's how I see this first paragraph, that they were deployed there and that they were engaged in these activities, in this Trnovo battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So they were in the Trnovo area. Does the OTP have a document showing their presence in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The OTP does not have any document, and the OTP does not have any information that this unit was ever in Srebrenica at that time, so based on information the OTP obtained during the investigation, regardless of the order we have seen from -- and it is from 10th of July, regardless of this order, Tomo Kovac's order, they were never -- they never came to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In order to have it clear on the record, you are referring to the Skorpions when you say this unit was never in Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please tell us now whether the OTP or you yourself have perhaps obtained information that members of the Skorpions group perhaps had found somewhere in the area these men that they executed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The OTP does not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the OTP have any information regarding the very first encounter between the Skorpions and these persons whom they executed? How did they come across them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to information we have, they first came in contact with them on the day -- on the morning when they were killed, so, and based on what I testified before, that should be sometimes between 12 and 20 of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the OTP investigate whether perhaps these persons were attempting to reach Sarajevo via Trnovo and then were arrested en route there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a quite long route around, and based on the knowledge and information in the possession of the OTP, most of the individuals, most of the Muslim men who left Srebrenica after the -- after its fall, was heading north towards Tuzla. Some of them also south towards Zepa. And these are the main routes which they took, and because of the statement of one of the relatives of those killed men, those men left Srebrenica and were heading north towards Zvornik. So it would be quite illogical that they would make such a big turn down to south, to Trnovo. So that's why Prosecution -- it's Prosecution's position, and of course I share this position with the Prosecution, that they should be captured somewhere close to Srebrenica, and indeed transported down to south.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the OTP introduced a document in this case showing that some of the people went to Serbia, some to Zepa, and yet others to Gorazde, in attempting to break through, and that the shortest route from Gorazde to Sarajevo is via Trnovo? Could it then mean that perhaps they had been arrested in Trnovo, given the fact that the exact location is not known and that the actual people who arrested them are not known? So if you have investigated anything along those lines, would you please share that information with us? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed you're right. Some people, and I didn't say about that, tried to -- and crossed the border, actually the Drina River and went into Serbia and were captured there, and then some of them returned back to RS, so indeed that was the case that some of them left Srebrenica also toward west. And when I said towards south, I meant towards Zepa and from Zepa then of course towards Gorazde. So these were the cases, yes, and the Prosecution is aware of those cases which were going south, but is not aware of any case to go that south or to go towards Sarajevo. So I would say towards Tuzla, towards Serbia, towards Zepa and Gorazde, towards Kladanj, these are the main routes where the people went.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the exact location of their arrest and by whom remains a secret to this day. Has the OTP investigated why this is still shrouded in secrecy and are there any special reasons underlying that situation? Perhaps I was not clear in asking this question. I can rephrase it and put it more briefly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I understand it but if you can rephrase it will be perhaps a little bit easier for me to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Has the OTP conducted any investigations to establish why the location and the time of the arrest and execution of these persons still remains a secret and why were these persons executed so far from Srebrenica, at a site so far from Srebrenica, and so near on the route to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The investigation was -- was conducted, and we wanted to get as many information as possible, and I will repeat myself once more. We wanted to get as much as possible, and as far as we can, but I can just repeat once more what -- what kind of information we have, how far we came, and my answer will be the same, how -- what kind of information the OTP has, I think I was quite clear already during my testimony. But no further investigation has been done regarding other issues, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua wants to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Tolimir. I apologise. Witness, I would like to return to the question put to you by Mr. Tolimir on page 28, line 4 of this transcript. He was asking what was the distance between Srebrenica and Trnovo. Trnovo is the place where these people were executed. So could you tell us what the distance is between Trnovo and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's -- and this is a rough estimation, of about 200 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Has the OTP investigated whether the killed people had ever been the subject of an exchange by their killers, as they were in touch with the opposite side, with the adversary side, in order to exchange them for whom they wanted from that side?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on information the OTP obtained during the investigation, they were just brought to this area one morning and, soon after, they were executed. So there is no information they were ever considered to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As it is the OTP's estimation that it was on the 18th, the day on which they were brought and killed, were there any people captured on the 18th on locations around Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't say on the date of 18th any time during my testimony. What I said was that they were most probably killed between 12th and 20th of July. When exactly they were captured and when exactly which date was that they were killed is not known to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you this in order for us to see whether they had been held somewhere up to the point and moment of their execution or had been brought from a place which is even farther away from Srebrenica, because if you know in locations around Srebrenica and in Srebrenica itself, up to the 20th, there had been no captives, no people taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people, so this is not actually -- this is not true that people were not kept around Srebrenica between these dates. We know that they were kept there and in the area in Bratunac, Kravica, and Nova Kasaba. Most of them during the 13th of July, 12th and 13th of July, but some of them even later, especially in Bratunac. So -- but if we go back to these particular six individuals, since we don't know when exactly they were captured, so we can't say exactly what happened to them when they were -- after they were captured actually, so and if they were transported down to Trnovo on that same day, few days after that, so a lot of information is missing here, I agree with you, and I would like to have more information on this case, these individuals, so as I told you I tried to obtain, to search for more information on them but I was not able to find any. So that's why we cannot be that exact, and exclude the possibility that they were kept somewhere, because we simply don't know when and where exactly they were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. I know that the OTP has presented information here about the place and time of execution so it can be seen that it was before the 20th. What I should like to know now is this: In your previous testimony, you said that there exists a witness who saw people being brought on buses from Srebrenica to Trnovo and taken from Trnovo back to Srebrenica. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you didn't understand or maybe it was misinterpretation. What I said is that these people were brought down from Srebrenica, from the area, wider area of Srebrenica to Trnovo, and when you asked me regarding where additional people might be since they were -- if there is information that they were brought by buses, so we assumed that many more would be transport down there, where those would be. And I replied to this question that we simply don't know, they might be somewhere around Trnovo, killed and buried and we don't know yet where, or they might be -- it's also possible -- transported back to the Srebrenica area. That was my response, I think, to your question, but I didn't say that we know that they were indeed transported back to Sarajevo -- to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise to you, but as this is a public trial, and as we all understand, we can appreciate that those who have lost their families would like to know that location, that is why I ask you whether there exists a witness who had seen them, because you did refer to a witness who saw them in your previous testimony, how they were coming there with their heads down, so I'm talking about that witness. I'm just asking you whether that is -- that faithfully reflects what you said in your previous testimony, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you able to give a reference? In my recollection I don't know if the witness said that, it would be helpful for the witness and the Chamber to find that portion in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My legal adviser should try to find it. I asked if you remember whether that means that some would be found there, and the witness said yes, some of the killed might be found there. And what I want us not to do is not to send any wrong information from this trial to the public. My legal adviser will try to find that reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may reply to you in this way. So, yes, we have this witness statement who told us that these people were brought to Trnovo. In relation to others, which might be brought down there and killed, we actually -- we simply don't know this information -- this witness did not provide us any additional information of any additional killings by the members of their units, so we don't know if any additional individuals were killed in that area, and subsequently buried, or just left on the ground like all the others, and since we don't have any additional exhumations carried out in this area, we don't -- we cannot confirm any of the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the transcript reference is 7037, page number 7037, and the date is 29 October. As well as the previous page, I believe, but I need to check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps it's possible to have that part on the screen. It will take a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Janc, for being really clear in his answer. I will give him another opportunity to repeat that for the general public, since we are in open trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, are you sure that this number is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. I didn't check whether it has been recorded properly, 7037. [In English] 7037. Here is Mr. Tolimir's question and then an answer about the buses. For example, it says, the -- [In English] "The OTP tried to obtain -- to obtain more corroborating statements in relation to the same issue," [Interpretation] and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, to which line you were referring?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7037 is the page number, and Mr. Tolimir's question features on lines from 3 through 6, and the witness's answer is on lines 7 through 17, and so on. And I believe that we have precisely that on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, we succeeded and perhaps we can -- the witness is able to read that part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, but I don't have it on the screen. So maybe I need to switch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The court usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And maybe it's just me, but I seem to have lost complete track of the question that Mr. Tolimir has put to the witness. I believe that it started out with the suggestion that the made had made a certain representation with respect to where these individuals that were -- or other individuals may have been killed. I don't see that in the transcript that is now on the screen. The only reference to that that appears to be close to the question, as I recall it, is an answer that the witness gave saying that the question was speculative and his answer was effectively speculation. And I don't see that that is -- if that's the reference that General Tolimir is going to, I just don't see how that is at all helpful to any material issue or any issue, frankly, before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I note the witness has read this part in the meantime and now you should put the relevant question to this part, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Since I don't speak English, and I can only remember what the witness said a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this. The witness who provided information to the OTP about Trnovo and the arrival of buses, did he observe that from a location in Trnovo or a location in Sarajevo? And was that witness familiar with both locations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness who provided it, he observed that from Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So how could he then know that the buses travelled from Sarajevo to Trnovo and back, and that that was repeated several times? I believe that's what the witness said. I'm sorry, I said Sarajevo instead of Srebrenica. The route was Srebrenica-Trnovo and back. Thank you, Aleksandar, for correcting me.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one was a member of the Skorpions unit, and this was known to him, being a member of this unit, and that's how he came across of this information. That's what he told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the OTP able to corroborate his words through any other witness, through any other piece of evidence? I don't speak English. I'm just allowing you to comment upon all that, and don't think that you can do me any harm by putting your comments forth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other individuals which were identified and interviewed by the OTP were reluctant to say where these individuals came from. So this is one of the individuals who told us how they were brought down there to Trnovo area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we are running out of time. We must have our first break. But before we do that, I will have to correct myself. I was recorded on page 7, line 11, to have said, exhibits P1150 and P1153. The correct reading should be P1150 through P1153. That means the exhibits P1150, 51, 52, and 53. Just for the record. We break now and resume 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we were talking about the so-called witness who allegedly saw the comings and goings and I would not belabour the point any further. I would just like to say that that witness belonged to the circle of those who participated in the killings of the six men, or, rather, I would like to ask you whether he belonged to that circle. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the member of the Skorpions unit but he was -- he did not participate in the killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was his statement credible in respect of other facts that he presented during his testimony? Did you investigate that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you talk about the statement as a whole, I think it is credible, yes, and also the fact regarding this particular information of -- in relation to the killings of these six men, I think it is credible, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: At page 35, just now you have said in answer to General Tolimir's question, whether the person was a member -- sorry, let me go back. Whether he belonged to that circle, meaning the circle of the Skorpions, and your answer was he was a member of the Skorpions unit but he did not participate in the killing. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to his statement but not only his statement, according to the statements of the others, and the problem is now because maybe we go into private session, I can tell you more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm not going to mention the person that has just been mentioned, but I'm going to have a question about the situation since that individual was not a participant in the killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was that person in the location when the killings were taking place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not at that location, at the spot where the killings took place, no. He was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was he in that village where his unit was? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was there, yes, according to his statement, he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he know that the video recording was commissioned? I suppose he must have known, hence the loaning of the camera. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He learned about this incident and that the incident was filmed later on, when the whole unit returned back to Croatia and when the camera was returned back to him, when he found the actual tape inside this camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it possible that those who perpetrated the crime by killing the six Muslims in Trnovo hid it from the rest of the group? Is it possible that they had been given a task to record all that on a camera? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As it was established, you know, they had made this filming on purpose, so they were aware of it and they wanted to do it and that's what it was done, so -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does this mean that the entire group did not hide from each other what they had done, that they did it openly and that they recorded it to meet the requirements of those that they had filmed it for?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they have made it openly because after they returned back to Croatia, indeed, several copies of this tape has been made and distributed throughout the members, and later on, the leader of this unit wanted all these tapes to be returned back so the -- but when I mean later on, you know, a few years after this event, and they wanted to destroy everything. And according to information the OTP has they have destroyed many of them but not all of them, and when I say that they had not made it public, that's why the OTP got possession of this tape only in 2004, which is nine years after the actual incident took place. So we can't say it was publicly known, so it was -- this incident and -- the existence of the tape itself was known to the limited number of the people, and that's why, in my opinion, it was not publicly known that this was -- this was done. So it was just for the benefits of the -- this certain unit, of the members of the unit, and their close circle, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You said that there were ten copies and that they made those copies and took them to Croatia. Did you investigate who the recipients of those copies were? And if you did, could you please tell us is it possible that perhaps one of the recipients of those copies was the original order issuer?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't say there were ten copies but several copies. So I don't know the exact number of how many copies. And recipients of these copies were basically the members of the Skorpions unit who were involved in this incident, and most of them, and again I'm talking about the statements which the people gave to the OTP, according to these statements, most of the tapes were indeed returned back to the head of this unit, and most probably destroyed. But not all of them, because if all of them would be returned back, the OTP would never get one of these copies, and according to the source from whom the OTP obtained this copy, this is the original tape which was -- copy of the original tape which was inside the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you try to establish whether, besides the participants in the events, anybody else received one of the tapes, and if they did, would they perhaps be on the list of the individuals who had ordered the killings? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The OTP tried to obtain also this information, but I think we don't have an information on who exactly received these tapes. So we know that some of the members of this unit received them. If any of the individuals who ordered this execution received them as well, that's what the Prosecution does not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you investigate whether anybody had the recording in their possession, if they had not participated in the incident, and if that was the case, could that perhaps be the trail to the order issuer? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the OTP endeavoured to obtain at least one additional copy or information who still have this additional copy of the tape. Just to be able to corroborate the other tape which we obtained from this source, meaning that, you know, that we indeed have everything what was filmed at that time, so we've never obtained any additional copy of this same video. This is the only one we have. And the same we don't have any information who might be having additional copies of this tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you this because in your statement, in paragraph 3, you say: "The copies of that film were subsequently cut in sheet." My question is this: Were copies made for each member or were the recipients of the copies hand-picked? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you tell us which statement of the witness you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mean statement. I meant document P1023, page 2, line 3, or, rather, second page, third paragraph, line 6. Thank you. Thank you. We can now see that on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, line 6, it is stated copies of that film were subsequently made in Sid. That is the previous page in English. The third paragraph. Can we see the previous page, please revert to the previous page in English. Paragraph 3. Thank you. In line 6, it reads: "Copies" -- My question is: Does the OTP have an accurate list of persons who were made available a copy of this film?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think the OTP has the exact list of the recipients of these copies. We for sure have some names, but this is based on the statement of the provider of this video to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone of the participants who have been convicted by national courts, had any of them been in any sort of contact or touch or liaised in any way, by telephone or otherwise, with members of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean General Staff of the VRS? If you mean that, we don't have -- I mean the OTP does not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Medici -- did Medic's immediate superiors, on their part, have any contact with the people who were convicted for events in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure she heard the question correctly. Could the accused kindly repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I've been asked to repeat the question. Did anyone of the immediate superiors of Medic and the participants in this crime, has the OTP registered any contacts between those persons with any people from the General Staff or any of those who participated in the events in Srebrenica who have stood trial before this Court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The OTP does not have any such information. They have been liaisoning through their superior with the minister -- or Deputy Minister of Interior, at that time, which was Tomo Kovac. He has been in contact with them. And according to information, I mean, his statement also, with some members of the government of the Republika Srpska at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have information whether at that time anyone of their superiors, conditionally speaking, had had any contacts with me as the accused here, either personally or via telephone?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently, the OTP does not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the OTP know whether any one of the participants in the event or any of their superior, whether immediate or otherwise, had come to Zepa during the relevant time when you indicated the events happened?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as before, the OTP does not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Have you investigated what exact level in the chain of superiority issued the order for the execution to be filmed? The exact chain of command hierarchical level.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've answered this question several times already throughout my testimony. So I explained how far the Prosecution got with the investigation, so we know that -- who executed these killings and no, we don't have any information on the superior level of the -- of this incident. So I can't say anything more than I already told during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please just tell us this: Are there any records about the routes via which the executed came to Trnovo? Is that something that is known?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no such records on it, and basically due to the fact that we don't even know where exactly they were captured and then picked up and brought down to the Trnovo area, so the Prosecution does not have this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us this: As the investigator, did you unequivocally or without any doubt obtain data and information that the actual shooting of -- filming of this event had been actually ordered by someone?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have no such evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And those two participants who said that they had to film it, who were looking for a battery, had they been tasked with making that film?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to their statements, they were tasked to do this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does this actually indicate the fact that prior -- prior to the killings, someone had issued an order for the execution?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Janc, for sharing with us your information. After having perused all these materials. This concludes my questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concludes my cross-examination as regards this part of Mr. Janc's testimony. I thank on behalf of the Defence, all the participants in this case, for helping us to understand one another, and I should also like to thank the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Are there other -- at the moment, not informed about the situation. Are there other parts of the examination-in-chief, when Mr. Janc testified, you intend to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Vanderpuye, can you help us?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think so, Mr. President. As you may recall, Mr. Janc also testified with respect to exhumations and the number of bodies that were recovered, association between mass graves, primary and secondary graves, et cetera, and I think that is what General Tolimir is referring to when he says -- when he is saying -- when he refers to this part of his cross-examination as opposed to the other parts of Mr. Janc's direct examination, which don't involve -- which, rather, involve the provenance and authenticity of the video footage that we offered into evidence prior to this part of the cross-examination. I should point out, though, that I do have some redirect examination, and with the court's permission, assuming that I've addressed Mr. Tolimir's position correctly, I'd like to proceed with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would first like to know what is the situation, and how do you -- how are your plans to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Gajic, you can help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, of course, this witness will appear again here to be cross-examined in connection with his report on DNA analysis, exhumations, and similar issues. We have already pointed out to the Trial Chamber that we have agreed with the OTP that that portion of the cross-examination shall be conducted after we have heard expert witnesses of the OTP who will also testify on exhumations, DNA analysis, anthropological analysis, et cetera. After we hear those witnesses, we shall proceed with our cross-examination of Mr. Janc on that subject. As regards this cross-examination, it focused only on the last portion of the statement given by Mr. Janc in the examination-in-chief. Precisely on those topics which Mr. Vanderpuye referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this update, or information respectively, or reminder respectively. Mr. Vanderpuye, your re-examination. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, the Chamber tried to figure out at which stage of the testimony of this witness we are currently, and I think the topic of this video, of the killing of the six Muslim men, that was part of your examination-in-chief and of the cross-examination, and now you are going to re-examine the witness on this topic solely; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And are there -- can you tell us about the situation with the other parts, like DNA analysis and mass graves? At the moment, we are a little bit lost. Are we still in the part of examination-in-chief or in the cross-examination of the witness to that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's a very fair question, Mr. President. I think, and my recollection is not always right, as you know, but I think that with respect to the DNA -- with the report of Mr. Janc, we had begun cross-examination on that specific issue. I can't remember how it was that it was interrupted but it was, and subsequently I believe we reached an understanding with the Defence about when they would resume the cross-examination. Okay. I'm -- I understand that Mr. Tolimir has gone three hours and 35 minutes into that cross-examination on that issue, the DNA, exhumation-related issues, that Mr. Janc first testified about. For whatever reason it was interrupted either by another witness or some circumstance and after that we reached an understanding with the Defence that he would resume this cross-examination after additional evidence had been received by the Trial Chamber concerning DNA, exhumation, demographic data, and that they would resume the cross-examination following that evidence.
